content.comment_body: Hello, I have an [product_name] Expansion Module with article number [article_no] that is damaged and not functioning. I am searching for a replacement module but have not been able to identify its successor. Could you help clarify which module would replace this product so I can proceed with the replacement? Thank you in advance.

All [product_name] expansion modules with article numbers ending in [article_no] have been discontinued by [company_name]. There are no direct successor modules for them. Current expansion modules (article numbers ending with [article_no]) are only compatible with [product_name] base modules of version [version_no]. The [product_name] version [version_no] has been available since September 2014, and the present model is the [product_name] [version_no] (article number [article_no]).
Hello [user_name], Can you clarify if the module [article_no] will work with the [product_name] CPU [article_no]? Thank you in advance.

No, all expansion modules with article number [article_no] are only compatible with [product_name] base modules of the [version_no] series. They do not work with earlier [product_name] versions. For further details, you can refer to the [company_name] product note issued in September 2014 regarding the delivery release for [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] software [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing challenges with compatibility and availability when trying to replace discontinued [product_name] Expansion Modules. There is confusion regarding which products are successors and whether they will work with existing base modules. Unclear communication on product lifecycle and module compatibility is resulting in uncertainty and potential device outages.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a simple replacement solution or information about successor modules for damaged expansions and expect compatibility details to be easy to find and transparent.
